name: Matbench: refractive index of inorganic crystals
description: Predict the DFT refractive index of 4764 inorganic crystals from their structure. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error over Matbench's five official cross-validation folds.

sources.locator: Petousis et al. (2017): high-throughput DFPT screening of inorganic compounds for dielectric and optical materials; source of the targets.
Dunn et al. (2020): Matbench v0.1 tasks, nested cross-validation protocol and MAE metric.
matbench_v0.1_validation.json (official folds) and stored per-fold predictions of published submissions (pinned commit).
Per-task Matbench v0.1 leaderboard (mean MAE over the five folds).

requirements.datasets: matbench_dielectric with the official folds. Fetched by python3 scripts/prepare_chemistry.py from pinned sources and verified by SHA-256 (catalog/chemistry-data-lock.json); not redistributed.

evaluation.benchmark: Matbench: refractive index of inorganic crystals
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) floats. Inputs are ordered crystal structures {'lattice': 3x3 lattice vectors as rows (Angstrom), 'species': element symbols, 'frac_coords': fractional coordinates per site}. Called once per official Matbench v0.1 fold (five calls, KFold(5, shuffle, random_state=18012019)), each in a fresh process that receives that fold's training inputs with targets and its held-out inputs without targets; info = {'task', 'input_type', 'target', 'unit', 'fold', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, RDKit and torch are importable; wall-clock limit 170 s per fold. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error in target units (minimize), the Matbench leaderboard metric

limitations: All targets are public in the Matbench files and every sample is a test sample of one fold; candidates or settings tuned on these folds overfit, so treat scores as development scores.

Leaderboard entries were trained without this task's limits (170 s and at most 4 CPU threads per fold, CPU only), so leaderboard values are reference points rather than targets attainable under the same budget.
Targets are DFT (DFPT) refractive indices with a few extreme values (up to 62) that dominate fold maxima; Materials Project data retrieved in 2019.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.

state_of_the_art.statement: Best mean MAE on the Matbench v0.1 leaderboard for matbench_dielectric: 0.2711 dimensionless (MODNet (v0.1.12)), read on 2026-10-10.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the refractive index of inorganic crystals from their structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Refractive index and dielectric response decide the use of materials in optics, photonics and capacitors; screening needs fast predictions before expensive calculations.

papers.title: High-throughput screening of inorganic compounds for the discovery of novel dielectric and optical materials
papers.primary_goal: Discover dielectric and optical materials by computing dielectric constants and refractive indices of many compounds.
papers.task_relation: The task predicts those refractive indices from structure.
